title: Weekly Markets Monitor - Bonds back in the room
gist: WGC's weekly monitor notes Treasuries rallying during the Nasdaq sell-off despite hotter inflation, sending a mixed signal for gold between bond competition for safe-haven flows and lower opportunity cost.

insights.claim: The 10-year Treasury yield fell during the current Nasdaq sell-off even though inflation recently surprised upward, resembling February 2025 and unlike July 2024, suggesting investors again look to bonds for safety as equity risks intensify.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Bond-equity hedging behavior is back, which matters for multi-asset positioning.

insights.claim: For gold the signal is mixed: renewed bond demand may compete for safe-haven flows, but falling yields lower gold's opportunity cost and could support it if the equity rout worsens.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Gold support depends on whether the equity rout deepens.

insights.claim: Middle East tensions intensified last week with attacks and continued Strait of Hormuz disruption pushing oil prices higher.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Energy supply risk remains the macro driver.

insights.claim: President Trump waived additional tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian energy.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Tariff relief eases pressure on buyers of Russian energy.

insights.claim: US consumer and producer inflation picked up in September, reviving expectations of further Fed tightening, while inflation also firmed in the euro area, India and China and China's trade surplus widened on strong exports.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Inflation is re-firming globally, keeping central banks hawkish.

insights.claim: Global equities closed the week mixed alongside lower US Treasury yields, a stronger US dollar and higher oil prices.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
